(a) In General.—Section 1244 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010 (Public Law 111–84; 123 Stat. 2541) is amended—
        (1) in subsection (a)—
            (A) by striking “fiscal year 2010” and inserting “fiscal year 2011”; 
            (B) by striking “pursuant to section 301(1)”; and 
            (C) by striking “$30,000,000” and inserting “$50,000,000”;  
        (2) in subsection (b)—
            (A) by striking “NATO Special Operations Coordination Center” and inserting “NATO Special Operations Headquarters”; and 
            (B) by striking “NSCC” and inserting “NSHQ”; and  
        (3) in subsection (c), by striking “NSCC” each place it appears and inserting “NSHQ”.  
    (b) Conforming Amendment.—The heading of such section is amended by striking “nato special operations coordination center” and inserting “nato special operations headquarters”.

fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments to an earlier funding authorization: it updates the fiscal year, raises the dollar cap, and renames a NATO entity. The tempting reading is that naming NATO, an outside body, signals coordination with a non-federal party. That fails because the text sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue before any federal decision.
fable.s: by striking “NATO Special Operations Coordination Center” and inserting “NATO Special Operations Headquarters”

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to a previous statute, updating fiscal years, funding amounts, and agency names. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The changes are purely administrative and legislative housekeeping.
qwen_block.s: Section 1244 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010 (Public Law 111–84; 123 Stat. 2541) is amended— (1) in subsection (a)— (A) by striking “fiscal year 2010” and inserting “fiscal year 2011”; (B) by striking “pursuant to section 301(1)”; and (C) by striking “$30,000,000” and inserting “$50,000,000”; (2) in subsection (b)— (A) by striking “NATO Special Operations Coordination Center” and inserting “NATO Special Operations Headquarters”; and (B) by striking “NSCC” and inserting “NSHQ”; and (3) in subsection (c), by striking “NSCC” each place it appears and inserting “NSHQ”. (b) Conforming Amendment.—The heading of such section is amended by striking “nato special operations coordination center” and inserting “nato special operations headquarters”.

opus.w: This section only makes technical amendments: it changes the fiscal year, removes a cross-reference, raises a dollar amount, and renames the "NATO Special Operations Coordination Center." The word "Coordination" might look like participation, but it is just part of a proper name. Nothing here requires or allows the federal government to consult anyone outside the government before making a decision.
opus.s: by striking “NATO Special Operations Coordination Center” and inserting “NATO Special Operations Headquarters”

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to a previous statute, specifically updating fiscal years, funding amounts, and the name of a NATO facility. It does not create any new requirement for the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or receive input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The mention of NATO is incidental to the renaming of a facility and does not constitute a participation mechanism defined in the instructions.
qwen_chat.s: (a) In General.—Section 1244 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010 (Public Law 111–84; 123 Stat. 2541) is amended— (1) in subsection (a)— (A) by striking “fiscal year 2010” and inserting “fiscal year 2011”; (B) by striking “pursuant to section 301(1)”; and (C) by striking “$30,000,000” and inserting “$50,000,000”; (2) in subsection (b)— (A) by striking “NATO Special Operations Coordination Center” and inserting “NATO Special Operations Headquarters”; and (B) by striking “NSCC” and inserting “NSHQ”; and (3) in subsection (c), by striking “NSCC” each place it appears and inserting “NSHQ”. (b) Conforming Amendment.—The heading of such section is amended by striking “nato special operations coordination center” and inserting “nato special operations headquarters”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions "NATO" (an international organization involving non-US governments), there is some form of participation. However, the text itself is merely an amendment to a previous statute, changing names and dollar amounts. It does not establish a new process for consultation, hearing, or advisory input. It is purely administrative/legislative housekeeping.
